page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-128 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured for general-purpose compute environments. Built on the Ampere Altra platform utilizing the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture, the instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.0 GHz with one execution thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present, and the instance includes no local NVMe storage, requiring attached network-based block volumes for persistent filesystem needs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in parallelized workloads. The 32 single-threaded cores excel in multi-threaded tasks, achieving 228.88 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 51.8 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, placing both metrics in the top tier of performance. In contrast, single-threaded processing exhibits lower relative performance, as seen in gzip compression and single-core decompression tests. Memory bandwidth remains steady at 173.39 GB/sec read and 78.82 GB/sec write for large uncached blocks. Standard synthetic benchmarks, including PassMark CPU and multi-core Geekbench, indicate consistent mid-tier execution across compute and database operations.

The absence of simultaneous multithreading provides predictable compute execution without resource contention between sibling threads on a single core. Because the instance relies entirely on remote storage, I/O-heavy applications must account for network storage latency and throughput boundaries. The hardware profile offers high core density and memory scaling without the expense associated with specialized accelerator hardware. These characteristics make the VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-128 well suited for horizontal web serving, microservices architectures, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed in-memory databases.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-128 is a balanced, general-purpose compute instance built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. Powered by 32 dedicated Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 3.0 GHz with one thread per core, the instance provides 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not bundle discrete GPUs or local NVMe storage, depending entirely on network block storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluations show strong capabilities in parallel operations, highlighted by top-quartile static web serving throughput and multi-threaded decompression, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded performance. Because each vCPU maps directly to an independent physical core, the platform eliminates noisy-neighbor effects common to hyperthreaded configurations. This resource allocation delivers predictable compute performance and strong resource density, making it a reliable infrastructure base for containerized applications, scalable web servers, CI/CD build farms, and distributed database services.
